explanation: A dense dial over running text, not a sparse detector. Every non-initial content token (word, subword, number, code identifier, CJK or other script) sits around 0.15-0.4 of max, so any text with three or more content words, or any code or formula, crosses 0.25 of max whatever its topic. It climbs to 0.45-1.0 of max on a token that repeats or closely parallels something earlier in the same context: the second 'neutral' after 'neutralise', '<|im_' after an earlier '<|im_', 'sin' after 'cos', a repeated 'Yes. No.' cycle. Predicted inactive (below 0.25 of max): the text's first token, sentence-final '.', newlines, very short texts (one or two words plus punctuation, such as 'Hello.' or 'Thank you very much.'), and texts made only of one repeated function word or punctuation mark ('the the the ...', 'of of of ...', ', , , ...', '. . . ...'), however long they are.
